clue.text: Praise for a good cook

definitions.meaning: the exclamation of approval given to someone who has achieved something
a steak or joint that has had a thorough cooking right through is cooked this way

explanation.surface: A compliment paid to a talented chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a good cook' reads as a skilled person, but here it is a noun for a thorough cooking, as meat gets when cooked all the way through.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a congratulation and the term for meat cooked thoroughly, with no pink left.

clue.text: It may be seen still on calm days

definitions.text: It may be seen still on calm days

parts.words: It may be seen still on calm days
parts.note: a wind-driven grinding building stands motionless when there is no breeze

explanation.surface: Something visible on a quiet, peaceful day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as 'even now'; it means motionless, as sails are with no wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill driven by sails needs moving air, so on windless days its sails stand still.

clue.text: A vital conclusion

parts.note: vital here means of life, so the conclusion is the close of a lifetime

explanation.surface: A crucial ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vital' reads as crucial, but it means 'of life'; the close of one's life is an old phrase for death.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old term for the last part of life, its final stage.

clue.text: Fools: they are, to make aeroplane varnishes.

definitions.meaning: the lacquers painted on the fabric skins of early aircraft to tighten and proof them

explanation.surface: Idiots are used to make the coating for aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope was the varnish brushed onto the fabric wings of early aeroplanes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stupid people and the lacquer that stiffened fabric aircraft wings.

clue.text: Kids make one feel the pinch

definitions.meaning: pincers or tweezers that grip and squeeze

explanation.surface: Children are expensive to raise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feel the pinch' means suffer hard-up times, as parents of children do; literally, pincers pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for small children and also names pincers that literally grip and squeeze.

clue.text: A girl has inside information for the meeting

definitions.note: the definition describes a list of business drawn up for a meeting, so it stands for a noun

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the next piece within it, as a container holds its contents

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A young woman has insider knowledge to bring to a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang, as in 'get the gen'. 'has inside' reads as having inside knowledge, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The list of items of business set out for discussion is what is prepared for a meeting.

clue.text: Almost sounds as if a nobleman is in debt in a big way

indicators.note: the spoken phrase is nearly but not exactly the same sound as the answer

parts.note: a grandee is a nobleman, and one in debt owes

explanation.surface: A lord who is heavily in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grandee owes' said quickly nearly matches the answer, so 'Almost' admits the match is inexact. 'in a big way' seems to describe the debt, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand, pompous and on a large scale, grandiose describes things done in an impressively big manner.

clue.text: Time when a thing appears distorted

indicators.note: the letters of thing are twisted out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: When things look odd in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges THING. The surface suggests darkness making objects look odd, which is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period of darkness, a time of day.

clue.text: The flower quarter is behind you, Jack

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like flower
north is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: The flower district is just behind you, sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a sailor (Jack Tar), so the definition is the nautical word for behind.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, towards the stern is the sailor's word for at the back.

clue.text: Did they really have the definition of "It " ?

definitions.text: Did they really have the definition of "It " ?

parts.words: Did they really have the definition of "It "
parts.note: refers to the saying that an ancient people had a word for it

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone truly defined a mysterious 'It'.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'The Greeks had a word for it', also a 1930 play and film title, so the clue asks if they truly had a definition of 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Hellenes are proverbially said to have had a word for everything.

clue.text: Score sheet used by the Bank of England ?

definitions.text: Score sheet used by the Bank of England ?

parts.words: Score sheet used by the Bank of England
parts.note: a score is written in musical notes, and the Bank of England prints banknotes, so both use sheets of paper for notes

explanation.surface: A sheet for keeping score at the central bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a tally, but it is a musical score written in notes; the Bank of England's banknotes are printed on special paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper is called by this name, and the phrase also fits paper for musical notes or for banknotes.

clue.text: Make departure in art, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the departing piece is placed within the word art

parts.note: to make a departure is to go

explanation.surface: An artist breaks new ground in art, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make departure in art' reads as a new artistic direction, and 'in a manner of speaking' as a mere aside, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the jargon or slang of a particular group, a special way of talking.

clue.text: Sporting encounters

parts.note: athletic or hunting gatherings where competitors come together are called by a word that also means comes across

explanation.definitionFit: Athletics competitions and hunt gatherings are known by this name, a noun from the verb for coming together.

clue.text: He has nothing to do with the word-perfect

definitions.text: He has nothing to do with the word-perfect

parts.words: He has nothing to do with the word-perfect
parts.note: a person who corrects texts finds no work in a text that is already perfect in every word

explanation.surface: Someone who has no time for those who know their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'word-perfect' suggests actors who know their lines; read literally, a text with every word perfect leaves a corrector of texts nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: An emendator is one who makes corrections to a text, so a flawless text needs none of his work.

clue.text: Old medical hangers-on

parts.note: bloodsucking worms clung to patients in old medicine, and the same word was an old name for doctors and now means parasitic people

explanation.surface: Elderly doctors who won't leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeches were applied to patients to draw blood, 'leech' was once a word for a physician, and a 'hanger-on' who sponges off others is also called one.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodsucking worms used in old medicine literally hang on to the skin, and the word now means parasitic people.

clue.text: It's hard coming down — cold, too

definitions.text: It's hard coming down — cold, too

parts.words: It's hard coming down — cold, too
parts.note: a pellet of ice that falls from the sky is hard and cold

explanation.surface: A tough descent in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's hard coming down' sounds like a difficult descent; it is a hard ice pellet falling from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen pellets fall in a storm, both hard and cold.

clue.text: He's too confused to be calm

indicators.note: the letters of the words he's too are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A man too flustered to keep his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges HESTOO, the letters of 'He's too'. 'calm' looks like an adjective after 'to be', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe is to calm someone, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Even a bachelor might have one-for sewing !

definitions.text: Even a bachelor might have one-for sewing !

parts.words: Even a bachelor might have one-for sewing
parts.note: a small sewing kit has an old name that also means a married woman at home

explanation.surface: An unmarried man might still keep a wife, to do his mending.
explanation.walkthrough: A small sewing kit of needles and thread is called a 'housewife' (said 'hussif'), so a bachelor can own one.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a pocket sewing kit is also the word for a woman running a home.

clue.text: Impatient injunction to keep going

definitions.meaning: read as two words, an order to take fewer breaks

explanation.surface: Someone impatient urges others to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word into 'rest less', an order to pause less often.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unable to settle, and split in two it commands fewer pauses.

clue.text: Under current control, mainly

parts.note: a boat at the mercy of the currents of the main, the open sea, is floating loose

explanation.surface: Things are under control, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under current control, mainly' reads as 'mostly under control'; split differently it is a vessel controlled by currents on the main, the sea, and so not moored.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat floating loose with no mooring or steering is carried along by the currents of the sea.

clue.text: Draughts may be fatal to it

definitions.text: Draughts may be fatal to it

parts.words: Draughts may be fatal to it
parts.note: draughts here are deep drinks, which kill off a need to drink

explanation.surface: Cold currents of air could be deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draughts' suggests cold air; it means gulps of drink, which put an end to the craving.
explanation.definitionFit: A craving for drink is ended by a long swallow.

clue.text: It takes some following in music

definitions.text: It takes some following in music

parts.words: It takes some following in music
parts.note: an opening piece of music is by nature followed by the main work

explanation.surface: A musical passage that is hard to keep up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes some following' suggests something difficult to follow; read literally, an introductory piece of music always has something following it.
explanation.definitionFit: An introductory movement comes before the main work, so something always follows it.

clue.text: Where the roadman keeps his tankard?

definitions.text: Where the roadman keeps his tankard?

parts.words: Where the roadman keeps his tankard
parts.note: a tankard is a drinking pot, and a road worker's natural cupboard would be a hole in the road

explanation.surface: Where a road worker stores his beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: A tankard is a pot, and a road worker deals with holes in the road, so a 'pot hole' is his storage place.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow worn in a road surface splits into a pot and a hole to keep it in.

clue.text: They're higher than is natural

parts.note: in music, notes raised a semitone above their natural pitch

explanation.surface: Things elevated beyond the normal level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'natural' is a musical term, a note neither raised nor lowered; raised notes are a semitone above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical notes raised by a semitone sit above the natural note.

clue.text: Not part of one's glad rags — on the contrary

definitions.text: Not part of one's glad rags — on the contrary

parts.words: Not part of one's glad rags — on the contrary
parts.note: a rough penitent's garment is the opposite of fine party clothes

explanation.surface: Something you would never wear when dressing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glad rags' are one's best clothes; a coarse garment worn as a penance is the reverse of glad.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse garment of goat's hair worn next to the skin as a penance is the opposite of festive finery.

clue.text: Sort of rubber — half in diamonds

indicators.note: the first half of the letters of the words in diamonds is taken

parts.note: the five letters come from halving the ten letters by count, so their running forwards through these words is a coincidence of that pick, not a hidden-word device

explanation.surface: A kind of eraser, half of it set with gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the first five of the ten letters of 'in diamonds'. 'rubber' is an eraser, as in the natural rubber of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: India rubber is natural rubber, used for erasers.

clue.text: Exercise round the grassland — so to the fold

indicators.note: the exercise abbreviation is placed around the grassland word

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercise
lea is a poetic word for grassland or meadow

explanation.surface: Sheep exercise around the meadow before going back to their pen.
explanation.walkthrough: PT is physical training, the British school term for gym class. 'fold' looks like a sheepfold beside the grassland, but it is a crease in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a crease made by doubling cloth back on itself.

clue.text: This house has the current issue

parts.words: This house has the current issue
parts.note: a ... house is a station issuing electric current

explanation.surface: This household has the latest edition of the magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current issue' sounds like the latest edition; it is electric current issuing from a power house, a generating station.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical energy is what flows as current from a generating station.

clue.text: This show needs firm backing

parts.note: a cowboy display where riders must keep a firm seat on bucking horses' backs

explanation.surface: A theatrical production that needs a solid sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm backing' sounds like financial support; here it is a rider holding firm on the back of a bucking horse or steer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a show of cowboy skills such as riding bucking broncos, where staying on the animal's back is everything.

clue.text: She made friends of the little people

definitions.text: She made friends of the little people

parts.words: She made friends of the little people
parts.note: the fairy-tale princess who lived with seven dwarfs

explanation.surface: A woman who befriended those of lower station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the little people' sounds like ordinary folk or fairies; it is the seven dwarfs of the fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale heroine sheltered in the cottage of the seven dwarfs and became their friend.

clue.text: Youngster most likely to get into a scrape?

definitions.text: Youngster most likely to get into a scrape?

parts.words: Youngster most likely to get into a scrape
parts.note: a young lad is called by an old slang word, and a razor is what scrapes a face

explanation.surface: The child who is always in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young shaver' is an old informal word for a lad, and a razor literally makes a scrape, so the mischievous boy is also the scraping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang calls a boy a young shaver, and a razor is the device that scrapes the chin.

clue.text: Niobe wasn't so materially sound

parts.note: the weeping mother of Greek myth was never dry-eyed, and cloth that is sound has no rips

explanation.surface: A mythical figure who was not well off.
explanation.walkthrough: Niobe wept endlessly for her slain children in Greek myth. 'materially sound' sounds financial, but it means cloth with no tears (rips) in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dry-eyed and, read as fabric, free of rips; the grieving Niobe was never without weeping.
